kurals.tr: Irunokku Ivalunkan Ulladhu Orunokku / Noinokkon Rannoi Marundhu
kurals.m: There are two looks in the dyed eyes of this (fair one); one causes pain, and the other is the cure thereof

kurals.tr: Kankalavu Kollum Sirunokkam Kaamaththil / Sempaakam Andru Peridhu
kurals.m: A single stolen glance of her eyes is more than half the pleasure (of sexual embrace)

kurals.tr: Nokkinaal Nokki Irainjinaal Aqdhaval / Yaappinul Attiya Neer
kurals.m: She has looked (at men) and stooped (her head); and that (sign) waters as it were (the corn of) our love

kurals.tr: Yaannokkum Kaalai Nilannokkum Nokkaakkaal / Thaannokki Mella Nakum
kurals.m: When I look, she looks down; when I do not, she looks and smiles gently

kurals.tr: Kurikkontu Nokkaamai Allaal Orukan / Sirakkaniththaal Pola Nakum
kurals.m: She not only avoids a direct look at me, but looks as it were with a half-closed eye and smiles

kurals.tr: Uraaa Thavarpol Solinum Seraaarsol / Ollai Unarap Patum
kurals.m: Though they may speak harshly as if they were strangers, the words of the friendly are soon understood

kurals.tr: Seraaach Chirusollum Setraarpol Nokkum / Uraaarpondru Utraar Kurippu
kurals.m: Little words that are harsh and looks that are hateful are (but) the expressions of lovers who wish to act like strangers

kurals.tr: Asaiyiyarku Untaantor Eeryaan Nokkap / Pasaiyinal Paiya Nakum
kurals.m: When I look, the pitying maid looks in return and smiles gently; and that is a comforting sign for me

kurals.tr: Edhilaar Polap Podhunokku Nokkudhal / Kaadhalaar Kanne Ula
kurals.m: Both the lovers are capable of looking at each other in an ordinary way, as if they were perfect strangers

kurals.tr: Kannotu Kaninai Nokkokkin Vaaichchorkal / Enna Payanum Ila
kurals.m: The words of the mouths are of no use whatever, when there is perfect agreement between the eyes (of lovers)
